title: The score that ranks classifiers and binners
meaning: Tools that only label sequence as plasmid or not (classifiers) are ranked by how many bases they label correctly (base-level F1). Tools that group contigs into plasmids (binners) are ranked by how correctly each base is placed in the right plasmid (length-weighted binning F1). Complete reconstruction (CPRR) is shown beside the binning score as the second measure.
if_changed: This is built into the scoring code. Changing the text here only records a different decision; the ranking will not change until the program itself is changed.

title: The score that ranks reassemblers
meaning: Tools that build new plasmid sequences are ranked by the share of each isolate's plasmids they reconstructed completely and accurately (isolate-level CPRR). Binning F1 is shown beside it.
if_changed: Built into the scoring code. Changing the text only records a different decision.

title: How sensitive complete-reconstruction scores are to the cut-off
meaning: The report also shows how the reconstruction score would move if the coverage and purity cut-offs were stricter or looser (0.80 to 0.99). It is for information and never changes a rank.
if_changed: Built into the code. It does not affect rankings.

title: Whether isolates with many plasmids dominate
meaning: Both versions of the reconstruction rate are reported: counting every plasmid equally, and averaging per isolate so that an isolate with many plasmids does not dominate.
if_changed: Built into the code. It does not affect rankings.

title: How reference sequences are called plasmid or chromosome
meaning: The main ranking uses the labels from the NCBI sequence report. The other two labelling schemes are used only to check whether the ranking would change.
if_changed: Changing it re-labels every reference, so every score changes. Results from before the change cannot be compared with results after it.

title: Which other labellings are used as a check
meaning: The ranking is repeated with the two other labelling schemes, and the report says how much the order changed.
if_changed: Built into the code.

title: How the reference assembly must have been built
meaning: Only references built mainly from long reads count for the main ranking. References built from short reads first are shown separately.
if_changed: Built into the code. See also the independence rule below.

title: What a tool scores when it crashes or gives no output
meaning: A tool that crashes or produces nothing on an isolate scores zero for that isolate and is still ranked. A tool cannot move up by failing on hard isolates.
if_changed: Built into the code. A different rule would change every ranking.

title: What happens when the computer, not the tool, fails
meaning: If the run was killed by the computer (out of memory, a timeout, a lost disk) it is re-run and not scored against the tool.
if_changed: Built into the code.

title: How many times a failed run is retried automatically
meaning: A tool that fails is run once more before it is counted as failed.
if_changed: A higher number gives flaky tools more chances and makes runs slower; it can change who fails.

title: How long one tool may run on one isolate
meaning: By default there is no limit. If you set one, a tool that runs longer on one isolate is stopped and counted as failed, and a failure scores zero for that tool. The limit is per tool per isolate, the same for every tool, not for the whole pipeline.
if_changed: A limit that is too short penalises slow tools unfairly (some tools take many hours on a large isolate, and a pipeline with many tools and many isolates can run for days). Set one only to stop a run that is truly stuck, and make it generous, for example 172800 seconds (two days). Enter none for no limit.

title: How species are weighted in the main score
meaning: The main score is the average of per-species averages, so one over-represented species cannot dominate. A species needs enough independent studies to be included.
if_changed: Built into the code.

title: How many independent studies a species needs
meaning: A species counts in the species-balanced score only when its isolates come from at least this many independent studies (or clonal groups).
if_changed: A lower number lets thinly sampled species into the main score; a higher number leaves more species out.

title: Smallest accepted sequence match
meaning: When a prediction is compared with the reference, an alignment below this identity is ignored.
if_changed: Changes every score slightly. Looser values reward sloppy matches.

title: Size above which a second chromosome is suspicious
meaning: A reference replicon labelled chromosome that is not the largest and is at least this long is flagged as a possible second chromosome (chromid).
if_changed: Changes which references are flagged for review; it does not change scores directly.

title: Size above which a plasmid is flagged as large
meaning: A plasmid at least this long is flagged, because it may really be a second chromosome.
if_changed: Changes which references are flagged for review.

title: Fewest independent studies for a confidence interval
meaning: An interval is only computed when the scores come from at least this many independent studies. With fewer, the report says the interval cannot be estimated.
if_changed: Built into the code. Lower numbers would give intervals that mislead.

title: Fewest independent studies for a significance test
meaning: A comparison test between two tools is only run with at least this many independent studies. With fewer, the smallest possible p-value is too large to be meaningful.
if_changed: Built into the code.

title: When tests are exact and when they are simulated
meaning: Up to this many independent studies the test counts every possible outcome exactly; above it, it samples outcomes at random.
if_changed: Built into the code.

title: Shortest accepted alignment
meaning: Alignments shorter than this many bases are ignored when predictions are compared with the reference.
if_changed: Changes every score slightly. The report shows how sensitive the ranking is to this value.

title: Smallest accepted alignment confidence
meaning: Alignments the aligner is not confident about (below this quality) are ignored.
if_changed: Changes every score slightly.

title: Smallest share of a contig that must align
meaning: A predicted contig must align over at least this share of its length for the alignment to count.
if_changed: Changes every score slightly.

title: How much of a plasmid counts as recovered
meaning: A plasmid counts as recovered when at least this share of it is covered by the prediction.
if_changed: Changes the recovery and complete-reconstruction counts for every tool.

title: How exact a plasmid must be to count as perfect
meaning: A plasmid is perfect when both its precision and its recall reach this value.
if_changed: Changes how many plasmids are called perfect.

title: When a plasmid is called fragmented
meaning: A plasmid is fragmented when a second bin holds at least this share of it.
if_changed: Changes how many plasmids are called fragmented rather than merged or missed.

title: When a plasmid is called missed
meaning: A plasmid is missed when the best bin recovers less than this share of it.
if_changed: Changes how many plasmids are called missed.

title: Shortest contig scored in the contig view
meaning: The contig-level view (shown beside, never used for ranking) ignores contigs shorter than this.
if_changed: Affects only the contig view.

title: Smallest match for the contig view
meaning: Minimum identity for a contig to be assigned in the contig view.
if_changed: Affects only the contig view.

title: Smallest coverage for the contig view
meaning: Minimum share of a contig that must align in the contig view.
if_changed: Affects only the contig view.

title: How similar two halves must be to call a double copy
meaning: A reference plasmid whose two halves match at least this well is treated as a head-to-tail double copy (a dimer).
if_changed: Changes which references are collapsed to a single copy.

title: How much each half must cover
meaning: Each half must align over at least this share to count as a double copy.
if_changed: Changes which references are collapsed.

title: Whether double copies are collapsed
meaning: 1 means a reference that is a double copy of a plasmid is reduced to one copy before scoring; 0 leaves it.
if_changed: Changes the reference sequence for affected plasmids and so their scores.

title: Read depth that supports an integrated element
meaning: A candidate plasmid integrated into a chromosome needs at least this read depth to be considered supported.
if_changed: Only affects an exploratory group of references.

title: Whether a candidate must form a circle
meaning: An unverified candidate needs a circular path in the assembly graph to be considered.
if_changed: Only affects an exploratory group of references.

title: How close to the best counts as near-optimal
meaning: A recommendation is near-optimal when its score is within this distance of the best tool for that isolate.
if_changed: Changes how often a recommendation is called good enough.

title: Smallest gain that justifies recommending per isolate
meaning: If always choosing the single best tool is within this distance of the perfect per-isolate choice, per-isolate recommendation is not worth it and the verdict says so.
if_changed: Changes when the recommender is switched on.

title: How bad a recommendation must be to count as failed
meaning: A recommendation that scores this much worse than the best tool is counted as a failure.
if_changed: Changes the failure counts in the recommender evaluation.

title: Lowest score at which a tool is still recommended
meaning: If the best expected score is below this value, no tool is recommended, because none is good enough.
if_changed: A lower value recommends weaker tools; a higher value recommends less often.

title: Difference too small to matter
meaning: Two tools whose scores differ by less than this are reported as practically equivalent.
if_changed: A larger value calls more pairs equivalent.

title: The test used to compare two tools
meaning: Two tools are compared with a permutation test on whole studies, with a second test beside it, and p-values are adjusted for the number of comparisons (Holm).
if_changed: Built into the code.

title: Distance below which a close reference exists
meaning: A distance report treats a plasmid as having a close relative in the reference set when the distance is below this value.
if_changed: Changes only the wording of that report.

title: The locked test set for the recommender
meaning: The recommender's test set is locked and may be evaluated once, so it cannot be tuned against.
if_changed: Built into the code.

title: Weights in the overall scorecard
meaning: How much each measure counts in the overall scorecard grade. The scorecard is an extra view and never changes a ranking.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv, then record the change here. Only the scorecard grades change.

title: Grade boundaries of the overall scorecard
meaning: The overall score cut-offs for excellent, good, moderate and poor.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only the scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for sequence identity
meaning: Cut-offs for grading sequence identity.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for mismatch rate
meaning: Cut-offs for grading how many mismatches there are per 100 aligned bases.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for insertion and deletion accuracy
meaning: Cut-offs for grading insertions and deletions.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Variant concordance and structural variants
meaning: No grading is applied: there is no independent set of true variants to compare with, so these two measures are shown as unavailable.
if_changed: Needs an independent truth variant set first.

title: Boundaries for reference coverage
meaning: Cut-offs for grading how much of the reference is covered.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for completeness and plasmid recovery
meaning: Cut-offs for grading reconstruction completeness and plasmid recovery.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for structural accuracy
meaning: Cut-offs for grading structural accuracy (an estimate from alignments).
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for circularisation
meaning: Cut-offs for grading whether circular plasmids were closed correctly.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for repeat resolution
meaning: Cut-offs for grading how well repeats were resolved.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for gene recovery
meaning: Cut-offs for grading how many genes were recovered.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for annotation agreement
meaning: Cut-offs for grading how well annotations agree with the reference.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for run time
meaning: Cut-offs for grading run time in seconds. They depend on the computer.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for memory use
meaning: Cut-offs for grading peak memory in GB. They depend on the computer.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Boundaries for success rate
meaning: Cut-offs for grading how often a tool finishes.
if_changed: Edit config/scorecard.tsv. Only scorecard grades change.

title: Fewest isolates for a scorecard
meaning: A scenario scorecard based on fewer isolates than this is marked as having too little data.
if_changed: Changes which scorecards are flagged.

title: Largest plasmid drawn as a circle
meaning: Plasmids longer than this are not drawn as circular maps in the report.
if_changed: Changes which plasmids get a map.

title: How structural checks are used
meaning: The extra structural check (SV-PRR) is shown beside the reconstruction rate and never used to rank tools.
if_changed: Built into the code.

title: Region around a resistance gene that must also be recovered
meaning: A resistance gene counts as recovered with its context when this many bases on either side are also covered by the same contig.
if_changed: Changes the context figure only; it never changes a rank.

title: Lowest reference quality allowed in the main ranking
meaning: References are graded 1 (best) to 3. The main ranking accepts grades 1 and 2; grade 3 is used only as a check.
if_changed: Allowing grade 3 would put weak references into the main ranking.

title: Which references are independent enough for the main ranking
meaning: A reference is independent when it was built mainly from long reads and was not corrected with the same short reads the tools are tested on. The main ranking uses only independent references. Partly independent ones are a first check, and all references are a second check.
if_changed: If you allow more kinds, the main ranking can include references that share information with the tools being tested, which flatters them.

title: Older on/off form of the independence rule
meaning: The older two-valued version of the rule above: independent only, or any. Kept so existing set-ups keep working.
if_changed: Choosing any accepts every kind of reference.

title: How confidence intervals are calculated when species are balanced
meaning: When the ranking averages per-species means (the usual headline), the interval uses a studentised cluster bootstrap: whole studies are resampled within each species and each draw is scaled by its own standard error. Without species balancing the cluster-robust t interval of the previous decision is still used.
if_changed: Changes the intervals of species-balanced rankings, not the scores or ranks. In the simulation it is as good as the alternative in every stratified design and clearly better when one species dominates, so reverting would make those intervals narrower than they should be.

title: How confidence intervals are calculated
meaning: The default is a cluster-robust t interval, which treats each independent study as one unit. Two other methods stay available and are measured beside it.
if_changed: Changes every interval, not the scores or ranks. The simulation shows no method is right for every situation.

title: When one study is too large for the default interval
meaning: If one study holds more than this share of the isolates, intervals switch to the percentile method, which the simulation found less bad in that situation.
if_changed: A higher value keeps the default interval longer, where it is known to be too narrow when one study dominates.

title: Fewest independent studies for the main ranking
meaning: The main ranking is only produced when its references come from at least this many independent studies. Otherwise the ranking is marked provisional.
if_changed: A lower value produces a main ranking from fewer studies, with intervals that cannot be trusted.

title: Whether a weaker ranking may replace the main one
meaning: 0 means that when no reference qualifies, the report says the main ranking is unavailable. 1 would silently show a ranking on all samples instead, with a warning.
if_changed: 1 can present a weaker result as the main one.
